title: The Sex Doll Market Is Booming
author: Julie Bindel
content:
![The Sex Doll Market Is
Booming](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/08/AP21062589188001.jpg)

On May 5, 2026, in Gwangju, South Korea, a twenty-three-year-old man named[
_Jang Yoon-
gi_](https://www.dailian.co.kr/news/view/1663542/%ED%9B%BC%EC%86%90%EB%90%9C-%EB%A6%AC%EC%96%BC%EB%8F%8C-%EC%86%8C%EC%9C%A0%EC%9E%90-%EC%9E%A5%EC%9C%A4%EA%B8%B0-%EC%97%AC%EA%B3%A0%EC%83%9D-2026?ref=compactmag.com)
stalked, sexually assaulted, and brutally murdered Lee Chae-won, a
[_seventeen-year-old female high school
student_](https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/society/society_general/1261300.html?ref=compactmag.com).
During the subsequent investigation, police discovered two "real dolls"--
hyperrealistic life-sized sex dolls--in the perpetrator's apartment. Both
dolls had been mutilated: their necks and breasts slashed by sharp weapons.
Criminal psychologists and prosecutors concluded that these mutilations had
served as a calculated, physical rehearsal of the violence he later inflicted
on his human victim.

This case serves as tragic, real-world illustration of what a [_growing
number_](https://campaignagainstsexrobots.org/papers/?ref=compactmag.com) of
feminist campaigners and scholars argue: that sex dolls encourage the
objectification of the female form while serving as a psychological catalyst
and practice tool for extreme sexual violence. This has led to calls for the
production, distribution, and use of sex dolls to be criminalized. Real life
sex abuse cases have amplified these calls in recent months. In addition to
Yoon-gi, there was the case of Jason Forbes in Australia. In February of this
year, Forbes was sentenced to seven and a half years when police disrupted his
plan to abduct a girl whilst posing as a police officer. Forbes was found to
be in possession of a child sex doll.

The first mass-produced inflatable sex dolls (little more than rubber
mannequins with painted facial features) [_became
available_](https://historycooperative.org/who-invented-blow-up-
dolls/?ref=compactmag.com), mainly through mail-order catalogues and sex
shops, in the 1960s. But from the 1990s onwards, manufacturers began using
latex, then silicone, to produce dolls that were far more realistic, with
articulated skeletons and other lifelike features. As Jo Bartosch and Rob
Jessel write in their 2025 book _Pornocracy_ , "The latest generation are not
only warm, fleshy and able to be manipulated into any sexual position--they
come integrated with artificial intelligence and synthesised speech for the
ultimate believability."

> "The market is flourishing."

Today, high-end sex dolls cost several thousand pounds, and can include
heating systems, AI-powered conversation, realistic facial expressions, and
simulated breathing. There are also removable orifices, and mouths fitted with
sucking motions. Buyers can choose breast size, hair color, and other physical
attributes. For those who can afford it, different heads can be attached to
the body of the doll, for a bit of variety. The market is flourishing. One
2025 [_estimate_](https://www.wiseguyreports.com/reports/sex-doll-
market?ref=compactmag.com) put the global value at $4.71 Billion.
